title: Effect of intensive blood-glucose control with metformin on complications in overweight patients with type 2 diabetes (UKPDS 34)
abstract: In overweight patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, metformin reduced the risk of any diabetes-related endpoint and all-cause mortality compared with conventional management, despite similar glycemic control. The benefit was not explained by glucose lowering alone.

title: Reduction in the incidence of type 2 diabetes with lifestyle intervention or metformin
abstract: In the Diabetes Prevention Program, lifestyle intervention reduced the incidence of type 2 diabetes by 58 percent and metformin by 31 percent compared with placebo in high-risk adults. Lifestyle modification was more effective than metformin overall.

title: Empagliflozin, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: In patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk, empagliflozin reduced the primary composite outcome of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke, driven mainly by a reduction in cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality.

title: Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction
abstract: Among patients with heart failure and a reduced ejection fraction, dapagliflozin reduced the risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death regardless of diabetes status. The benefit was consistent across the studied subgroups.

title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control
abstract: Targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg reduced the rate of cardiovascular events and death compared with a target of less than 140 mm Hg in high-risk adults without diabetes. Serious adverse events of hypotension and acute kidney injury were more common with intensive treatment.

title: Rosuvastatin to Prevent Vascular Events in Men and Women with Elevated C-Reactive Protein
abstract: In apparently healthy adults with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and normal LDL cholesterol, rosuvastatin reduced the incidence of major cardiovascular events. The trial supported statin use based on inflammatory risk.

title: Effects of an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor, ramipril, on cardiovascular events in high-risk patients
authors: The Heart Outcomes Prevention Evaluation Study Investigators
abstract: Ramipril reduced the rates of death, myocardial infarction, and stroke in high-risk patients with cardiovascular disease or diabetes plus one additional risk factor. The benefit was larger than expected from blood-pressure reduction alone.

title: Overall Survival with Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab in Advanced Melanoma
abstract: In previously untreated advanced melanoma, the combination of nivolumab and ipilimumab improved overall survival and progression-free survival compared with ipilimumab alone, at the cost of more frequent grade 3 or 4 immune-related adverse events.

title: Pembrolizumab versus Ipilimumab in Advanced Melanoma
abstract: Anti-PD-1 therapy with pembrolizumab prolonged progression-free and overall survival and was associated with fewer high-grade adverse events than ipilimumab in patients with advanced melanoma.

title: Final report on the aspirin component of the ongoing Physicians' Health Study
authors: Steering Committee of the Physicians' Health Study Research Group
abstract: Low-dose aspirin reduced the risk of first myocardial infarction in healthy male physicians but did not reduce cardiovascular mortality and was associated with a small increase in bleeding.

title: Statins and risk of incident diabetes: a collaborative meta-analysis of randomised statin trials
abstract: Statin therapy was associated with a modestly increased risk of new-onset diabetes, an effect that was strongest in trials of older participants. The absolute cardiovascular benefit outweighed the small diabetes risk in most patients.
